To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the social identity theory can be applied to serious leisure, that football fans have a strong sense of group membership, and that the four behaviours identified by this theory are present in football fans.

(1) football fans are a highly committed group who engage in a range of behaviours to compensate for their lack of control over the team they support, (2) the behaviours of in-group favouritisation, out-group derogatation, unrealised optimisim, and voice are all important to football fans, and (3) the model of serious leisure presented here is a useful way to explain why people engage in activities that appear to be unrewarding.

serious leisure participants engage in four compensatory behaviours (i.e., in-group favoritism, out group derogation, unrealistic optimisim, and voice) that help them to maintain their participation despite the costs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a particular form of social behaviour, that which is engaged in for its own sake.
the social psychological factors that contribute to the development and maintenance of a serious leisure identity.
a particular type of social behaviour – that of football random, and how it is that people engage in such behaviour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the serious leisure identity is a social identity, which is based on a social category, and which is formed and maintained by the social processes of in-group favouritisation, out-group derogations, voice and unrealistic optimism.
the model of serious leisure identity presented here is a model of how people can and do maintain their serious leisure identity in the face of what may be perceived as a lack of rewards.
football fandom is a serious leisure activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in the social and psychological consequences of participation in leisure activities.
serious leisure participation is a complex process that involves a number of factors, which are inter-related.
we have demonstrated the importance of a social identity approach to understanding serious leisure participation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the serious leisure model of participation is not complete until it incorporates the social identity perspective.
the serious leisure model can be extended to include a social identity approach to explain why people continue to engage in such activities.
serious leisure is a form of social identity.
